'''''Mesembryanthemum nodiflorum''''' is a species of [[succulent plant]] in the genus ''[[Mesembryanthemum]]'' known by the common name '''slenderleaf iceplant'''. It is the [[type species]] for the [[genus]]. It is native to [[South Africa]]<ref>{{cite web |title=Population Genetics Reveals the Invasion Pathways of Mesembryanthemum nodiflorum in North America |url=https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/full/10.1002/ece3.72262 |publisher=[[Ecology and Evolution]] |access-date=15 November 2025}}</ref> but can also be found in coastal areas of the [[Mediterranean Basin]], [[Macaronesia]], and [[Middle East]]<ref>{{cite web |title=M. nodiflorum |url=http://www.floraiberica.es/floraiberica/texto/pdfs/02_047_05_mesembryanthemum.pdf |publisher=[[Flora Iberica]] |access-date=12 July 2021}}</ref>. It is known in many other places as an [[introduced species]] and sometimes an [[invasive species|invasive weed]], including several regions of [[Australia]], parts of the western [[United States]] and adjacent [[Mexico]], and some Atlantic islands.

''M. nodiflorum'' is a usually [[annual plant|annual]] [[herb]] forming a mostly prostrate clump or mat of stems up to a maximum of about 20 centimeters in length. The small stem branches are lined with knob-like cylindrical fleshy leaves up to 2 centimeters long. The herbage is green to bright red and visibly bumpy with shiny, bubble-like [[Plant cuticle|papillae]]. Flowers are solitary or borne in loose clusters. Each is about half a centimeter wide with many narrow to thready white or pale yellow petals. The fruit is a capsule which opens when it becomes wet, releasing seeds.
